subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: Should internal OpenClaw agent turns add strict tool-call enforcement for clearly tool-required requests, and should that policy be default behavior or opt-in per agent/model?
rationale: Current main intentionally mixes warning-only diagnostics, bounded text-tool promotion, and Gateway-only HTTP tool_choice enforcement, so tightening the internal loop changes both security posture and local-model compatibility.

options.title: Add opt-in strict enforcement
options.body: Introduce a bounded strict policy for explicitly tool-required turns while preserving the current compatibility behavior by default until maintainers approve a default change.

options.title: Make strict behavior the default
options.body: Fail or retry text-only tool-required turns across internal agent runs, accepting the upgrade risk as a stronger security default.

options.title: Fold into response gates
options.body: Defer this to the broader pre-response enforcement design so tool-call enforcement and claim-vs-ledger checks share one policy model.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in strict enforcement
recommendation.body: Introduce a bounded strict policy for explicitly tool-required turns while preserving the current compatibility behavior by default until maintainers approve a default change.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the agent-core dispatch boundary and security/default tradeoff where recent relevant history points to steipete.
